title: Constitution of the Republic of Singapore (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Constitution of the Republic of Singapore (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Judicial Service Bill debate
sections.summary: The Bill establishes a separate Judicial Service with a new Judicial Service Commission and makes consequential changes to the Legal Service.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Members can raise questions or express their views on both Bills during this debate.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We would still have the formal Second Reading of the Judicial Service (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill, to ensure that the necessary procedural requirements are dealt with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In essence, the Bill will: (a) establish a separate Judicial Service, overseen by a new Judicial Service Commission (JSC); and (b) make consequential changes to the Legal Service, which will be overseen by a reconstituted Legal Service Commission (LSC).

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We have consulted the President on the amendments, some of which affect her discretionary powers.

sections.label: Legal Service Officers at Independence
sections.summary: At the time of Independence, there were only 45 Legal Service Officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: At the time of Independence, we only had 45 LSOs.

sections.label: Legal Service Officers today
sections.summary: Over 800 Legal Service Officers now serve in various crucial roles, and their work contributed to recognition of the legal system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The work of many Legal Service Officers has contributed significantly to the recognition which our legal system has obtained as being among the best legal systems in the world.” Today, over 800 LSOs serve in various crucial roles.

sections.label: 2020 MinLaw public perception survey
sections.summary: A 2020 MinLaw survey found strong positive perception of Singapore's legal system and institutions among residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: A 2020 public perception survey by MinLaw found that there is a strong positive perception of our legal system and institutions among Singapore residents: 95% of respondents agreed that we are governed by the Rule of Law; 90% had trust and confidence in our legal system and agreed that we had an efficient legal system; around 90% had a positive view of our Courts and of AGC.

sections.label: AGC COVID-19 advice requests
sections.summary: In the first half of 2020, AGC received over 1,300 COVID-19 related requests for advice and responded to most within 24 or 48 hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In the first half of 2020 alone, AGC received over 1,300 COVID-19 related requests for advice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It responded to 69% of these requests within 24 hours and 78% of these within 48 hours.

sections.label: Government decision after consultations
sections.summary: After studying the matter and discussing it with the Chief Justice and Attorney-General, the Government decided it can take this step.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: After studying the matter further and discussing the matter in detail with the Chief Justice and the Attorney-General, the Government decided that we can take this step.

sections.label: Legal Service growth since 2014
sections.summary: The Legal Service has grown significantly since 2014, with 815 officers as of July 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Legal Service has, since 2014, also grown significantly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It had, as of July 2021, 815 officers.

sections.label: Establishment of Singapore Judicial Service
sections.summary: Clause 6(a), read with clause 26(1), establishes the Singapore Judicial Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Clause 6(a), read with clause 26(1), establishes the Singapore Judicial Service.

sections.label: CJ and AG as Presidents
sections.summary: The CJ will be President of the JSC and the AG will be President of the LSC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The CJ will be the President of the JSC and the AG will be the President of the LSC.

sections.label: Replacement of two Personnel Boards
sections.summary: Two PBs operating since 1995 were replaced by the Judicial Branch and Legal Branch Special Personnel Boards, overseeing most HR functions for LSOs up to Superscale Grade 3.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The two PBs that had been operating since 1995 were replaced by the Judicial Branch Special Personnel Board and the Legal Branch Special Personnel Board, which have been in operation since that time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: These two new PBs respectively oversee most human resource functions in respect of LSOs in the Judicial Branch and LSOs in the Legal Branch, up to Superscale Grade 3.

sections.label: Smaller Services after restructuring
sections.summary: Post-restructuring, the Services will be smaller, with about 200-plus officers in the Judicial Service and 500-plus in the Legal Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Post-restructuring, the sizes of the Services will also be smaller – about 200-plus officers in the Judicial Service and 500-plus for the Legal Service.

sections.label: Commission delegation limits and PB appointments
sections.summary: The Commissions may not delegate functions on senior officers at or above a threshold grade and discipline and dismissal, and PB member appointments remain subject to the President's concurrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Commissions may not delegate functions and powers relating to (a) either senior officers at or above a threshold grade; and (b) discipline and dismissal of any officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The appointment of members to any PB remains subject to the President's concurrence, as is the case today.

sections.label: Joint regulations for personnel functions
sections.summary: Articles 111F and 111N let the JSC and LSC make joint regulations for the other Commission to exercise personnel management functions over officers in prescribed posts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To facilitate this, Articles 111F and 111N, for JSC and LSC respectively, allow them to make joint regulations to provide that their personnel management functions over officers holding prescribed posts may be exercised by the other Commission.

sections.label: Bill inserts Judicial Service terms
sections.summary: The Bill inserts terms like Judicial Service Officer, Judicial Service Commission and Singapore Judicial Service into affected Acts so they apply to the Judicial Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Bill inserts terms, such as "Judicial Service Officer", "Judicial Service Commission" or "Singapore Judicial Service" into the affected Acts, where appropriate, such that Acts which apply in relation to the Legal Service will also apply to the Judicial Service, and Acts that apply in relation to the LSC will also apply to the JSC and, finally, Acts that apply in relation to LSOs will also apply to JSOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I stand in support of the Bills and the restructuring of our Legal Service into the separate Judicial Service Commission and Legal Service Commission.

sections.label: Transitional provision for existing officers
sections.summary: Under clause 26, the transitional provision, existing legal service officers will be allocated or re-deployed according to the posts they hold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In relation to clause 26 of the Bill, which is the transitional provision, existing officers in the legal service will be allocated or re-deployed according to the posts that they are holding.

sections.label: Judiciary commissioners appointed Supreme Court judges
sections.summary: Three judiciary commissioners have recently been appointed judges in the Supreme Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Recently, three judiciary commissioners have been appointed judges in the Supreme Court.

sections.label: Rotation between JSC and LSC officers
sections.summary: The speaker proposes flexibility or a fixed rotation between JSC and LSC officers in the early years of their careers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, the talent for our judiciary and the Bench must be built up internally as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I would propose that despite the separate arms being set up with the Legal Service Commission (LSC) and the JSC, that there should still be some flexibility or a fixed rotation between JSC and LSC officers in the early years of their career.

sections.label: Syariah law and Muslim community cases
sections.summary: Courts deal with sensitive Muslim community cases including Syariah law, AMLA, wakaf and faraidh, and the speaker suggests studying a broader framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Apart from commercial or civil cases, our courts also deal with cases involving sensitive issues that affect all walks of life in our Muslim community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: These include the interpretation of Syariah law issues, such as the interpretation of the Administration of Muslim Law Act (AMLA), wakaf or Islamic inheritance law (faraidh), as well as marriage or inheritance law for Muslims which are sometimes heard before the High Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In my maiden speech in Parliament, I have suggested how a more comprehensive arbitration process or legal framework can be studied to deal with cases of wakaf or estate disputes in our community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This can be done by broadening the jurisdiction of the Syariah Court or deepening the specialisation of our civil courts to handle such cases.

sections.label: Civil courts and MUIS opinions
sections.summary: Civil courts are not obliged to seek MUIS opinions on Islamic law, and the speaker suggests JSC members handle Syariah Court cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Civil courts, when faced with questions of Islamic law, are not obliged to seek an opinion from MUIS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Therefore, I think it is timely for the Government to set up the Judicial Service Commission (JSC).

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: My recommendation is for suitable JSC members to be seconded or take turns handling Syariah Court or Syariah Appeal Board cases to build their understanding and knowledge.

sections.label: Judicial Service Commission Bill support
sections.summary: The Workers' Party supports Constitution amendment Bills creating a separate Judicial Service Commission, with the AG heading the LSC and the CJ heading the JSC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party supports this move and indeed the Constitution of the Republic of Singapore (Amendment) Bill for these changes as this will among other things, promulgate even greater judicial independence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Bills proposed the setting up of a Judicial Service Commission (JSC) separate from the existing Legal Service Commission (LSC).

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Under the new arrangements, pursuant to the Bills, the AG will take over as the president of the LSC and the PSC chairman assume the newly considered role of Vice President.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The CJ shall be the President of the new JSC, while the PSC Chairman assumed the newly considered role of the Vice President, together with two other members, each nominated by the CJ, the PSC Chairman and the Prime Minister.

sections.label: Career tracks after JSC restructuring
sections.summary: The speaker asks how career tracks will differ after restructuring and how changes will enhance the separate Judicial Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I hope and have confidence that, with a dedicated JSC, our Judiciary and judicial officers can continue to rise to these challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I know the Minister touched on some aspects of this earlier, but, essentially, I would like to know how different will the career tracks be after the restructuring, and how will the changes enhance the new and separate Judicial Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Will there, for example, be a default career progression plan, planned under each of the Services' Commission and transfers across to the other will only be catered upon request by an officer, or by the management of either services?

sections.label: Remuneration frameworks for Judicial and Legal Services
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether remuneration frameworks will be differentiated between the Judicial Service and Legal Service tracks after restructuring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Next, I would also like to ask whether there are plans to differentiate the remuneration frameworks of the Judicial Service and the Legal Service tracks, to account for the differences in specialisation after the restructuring.

sections.label: Constitutional amendments creating separate JSC
sections.summary: Three months later, amendments to the Constitution are being considered to create a separate JSC from the LSC, planned for January 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As it turned out, just three months later, we are now considering these amendments to the Constitution to create a separate JSC out of the current LSC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If these amendments are passed, the plan is to put them into effect in January 2022.

sections.label: Pew Research Centre Report findings
sections.summary: The speaker says this may explain Singapore's performance in the Pew Research Centre Report dated 21 October 2021 on 17 advanced economies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Perhaps, this explains why Singapore did well in the Pew Research Centre Report dated 21 October 2021 which conducted research in 17 advanced economies, including Singapore, to identify whether citizens in these economies want significant changes to their political system.

sections.label: Singaporeans satisfied with democracy
sections.summary: 82% of Singaporeans said they are satisfied with how democracy works here, against an overall median of 57%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Eighty-two percent of Singaporeans said that they are satisfied with the way democracy is working here, compared to an overall median of 57%.

sections.label: Sedition Act repeal and JSC amendments
sections.summary: The Government has repealed the colonial-era Sedition Act and is moving Constitutional amendments with bipartisan support to create an independent JSC overseeing judicial service officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Since then, this Government has repealed the Sedition Act, which was introduced during the colonial times to rein in discontent against the Government and it is now moving these Constitutional amendments which will enjoy bipartisan support to create an independent JSC to oversee judicial service officers.

sections.label: COVID-19 pandemic Bills passed
sections.summary: During the COVID-19 pandemic last year, 12 wide-ranging Bills had to be passed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In the course of the COVID-19 pandemic last year, we had to pass 12 wide-ranging Bills.

sections.label: Reconstituted LSC and legal service officers
sections.summary: With the LSC split into a JSC and a reconstituted LSC, the reconstituted LSC should keep attracting top talent and hasten specialisation of Legal Service Officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: He was also inducted as a Young Global Leader by the World Economic Forum in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: We must ensure that with the split of the current LSC into a JSC and the reconstituted LSC, the reconstituted LSC should continue to attract and retain its fair share of top talent with the right set of values.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The Legal Service Officers of the Legal Branch perform vital roles in providing legal advice to the Government and playing their role in the administration of justice and helping to uphold of the rule of law in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: With the reconstituted LSC, there is an opportunity to hasten the pace of specialisation of the LSOs to keep up with the demands of their respective jobs and the ever-rising expectations of Singaporeans.

sections.label: LSC and JSC as twin pillars
sections.summary: The reconstituted LSC must stand with the JSC as twin pillars attracting and developing public legal sector talent to meet Singaporeans' expectations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The reconstituted LSC must stand shoulder to shoulder with the JSC as twin pillars in attracting and developing the best human resource talent in the public legal sector that will continue to meet the high expectations of Singaporeans well into the future.

sections.label: Trust and rule of law rankings
sections.summary: An IPS study showed 81% trusted the Government, 82% the Courts and 80% the Civil Service, with Singapore ranked in rule of law and judicial independence indices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Results released in March this year from an IPS study showed that 81% of the public had a great deal or quite a lot of trust in the Government; 82% said this of the Courts, and 80% said this of the Civil Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the 2020 World Justice Project Rule of Law Index measuring the rule of law in countries, Singapore was placed 12 out of 128 countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the 2019 World Economic Forum Global Competitiveness Report, Singapore was ranked 14 out of 141 countries for judicial independence.

sections.label: PSC Chairman as Vice-President
sections.summary: The Chairman of the PSC will be Vice-President of both the LSC and JSC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, the Chairman of the PSC will be the Vice-President of both the LSC and JSC.

sections.label: Legal Service Officers numbers
sections.summary: The 2020 Legal Service Commission Annual Report stated 806 Legal Service Officers as at 31 December 2020, with 224 judicial and 582 legal branch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In the 2020 Annual Report of the Legal Service Commission, it was reported that there are 806 Legal Service Officers (LSOs) in service as at 31 December 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Of these 806 LSOs, 224 were in the judicial branch and 582 in the legal branch.

sections.label: State Courts caseload 2020
sections.summary: The Singapore Courts Annual Report 2020 stated the State Courts had 187,016 cases in 2020, including 143,728 criminal, 31,189 civil and 12,099 community and tribunal-related cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Based on the Singapore Courts Annual Report 2020, the caseload of the State Courts was a total of 187,016 cases in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Out of these 187,016 cases, 143,728 are classified as criminal cases, 31,189 are classified as civil cases and there are 12,099 community and tribunal-related cases.

sections.label: Judicial officers and Judicial Services Commission
sections.summary: The passage discusses judicial officers' exposure and cross-service secondments, and states the Bills set up a Judicial Services Commission overseeing State Courts and Supreme Court judicial officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Judicial officers in the Family Justice Courts would have to deal with litigants sensitively, especially where there are young children involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: However, I am glad to hear the Minister's confirmation that cross-service secondments will continue to be available on application where useful, to provide selected officers with cross-service experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: For example, if a judicial officer in the Family Court wishes to seek a posting to MSF to better understand how family disputes can be resolved, surely that kind of cross-postings should be encouraged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Similarly, a legal officer who had served as a prosecutor or a lawyer who had previously worked as a litigation lawyer is better placed to understand the adversarial nature of disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I would also submit that all our judicial officers must have some wide exposure to community work and more depth of experience in life before being appointed as judicial officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Even as we position our legal service and judicial service officers as what former Chief Justice, the late Mr Yong Pung How, described as the “premier service” in the public sector, I hope that we also remind our judicial officers on the need to remain humble as they serve the wider society in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: These Bills involve the setting up of a Judicial Services Commission in Singapore which will oversee the judicial officers in both the State Courts and the Supreme Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Commission’s role includes determining the appointment, confirmation, placement on permanent establishment, promotion, transfer, disciplinary control and dismissal of judicial officers.

sections.label: Chief Justice and Attorney-General roles
sections.summary: The Chief Justice will be President of the Judicial Services Commission, and the Attorney-General will be President of the Legal Services Commission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Related to these changes, the Chief Justice, who was previously President of the Legal Services Commission, will now be President of the Judicial Services Commission, while the Attorney-General will now be President of the Legal Services Commission.

sections.label: Cross-postings under separate commissions
sections.summary: The passage notes a perception the judicial service is more desired and asks whether cross-postings will be more difficult with different commissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There is also a perception that the judicial service would be the more desired branch and, in the past, those in other parts of the legal service may aspire to be judicial officers if they performed well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, while I note that the separation of functions does not prevent cross-posting of officers, and the Minister in his introductory statement has stated secondments will be available, will such cross-postings be more difficult, now that there are different commissions governing both?

sections.label: Subordinate court definition in Bill
sections.summary: The term "subordinate court" in clause 26 has the same meaning as Article 93 of the Constitution, including State, Family and Youth Courts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The term "subordinate court" as used in clause 26 of the Bill has the same meaning as that in Article 93 of the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, it includes the State Courts, the Family Courts and the Youth Courts.

sections.label: No limits on JSC LSC reappointment
sections.summary: There are no limits on the reappointment of JSC and LSC members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The short answer to Mr Louis Ng is no.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There are no limits on the reappointment of JSC and LSC members.

sections.label: No Chief Justice or AG nominations
sections.summary: The intent is not to have the Chief Justice nominated to the LSC or the Attorney-General nominated to the JSC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I think Mr Dennis Tan also raised this point and what I have just said will also answer the query he had raised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I should also add to Mr Tan's question that the intent is not to have the Chief Justice nominated to the LSC or for the Attorney-General to be nominated to the JSC.

sections.label: State and Family Courts caseload
sections.summary: Between 2018 and 2020, the State Courts and Family Justice Courts handled an average of over 292,000 cases yearly, with clearance rates above 100%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The cases are getting more complex; not just more but also more complicated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And just to give Members a sense, between 2018 and 2020, the State Courts and Family Justice Courts collectively dealt with an average caseload of more than 292,000 cases each year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: What is also commendable is that, in these three years at least, the State Courts have consistently achieved a total case clearance rate of more than 100% each year, which means that the number of cases they clear exceeds the number of new cases that are filed each year.

sections.label: Secondments framework and engagement
sections.summary: A workgroup was set up with at least five townhalls and engagement with Legal Service Officers, who wanted secondments to continue for wider experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked about the secondments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I mentioned that in the two Articles 111F and 111N., and the framework here is to jointly develop a framework for cross-seondings secondments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There was a workgroup that was set up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There were at least five townhalls, significant engagement with Legal Service Officers, and they expressed a desire for secondments to continue; to continue to allow them to be seconded so that they can, as Mr Lim puts it, gain a far wider breadth of experience so that this will come to bear positively in the discharge of their services.

sections.label: Second Reading voting results
sections.summary: There were 85 Ayes, 0 Noes and 0 Abstentions, and the Second Reading was carried by not less than two-thirds of Elected and Non-Constituency Members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I will now proceed to declare the voting results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: There are 85 "Ayes", 0 "Noes", and 0 "Abstentions".

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Second Reading of the Bill has been carried by the votes of not less than two-thirds of the total number of Elected and Non-Constituency Members of Parliament.    .

sections.summary: The Third Reading of the Bill was carried with 85 Ayes, 0 Noes and 0 Abstentions, by at least two-thirds of Elected and Non-Constituency Members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I will now proceed to declare the voting results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
